text: What's the best place for a first date? Let me break it down. Guys, once again, simplify, don't complicate. A great first date isn't about being flashy or doing something crazy. The most effective setup is simple. A cozy bar, ideally with a sofa, nice but not too loud music, and an atmosphere where you can both relax, have a drink, and actually talk. Evenings after work or on the weekends are perfect. Skip mornings or afternoons. The lady may have plans later in the day and it's hard to fully relax when she's already thinking ahead. The earliest you should set a date is around 6pm. Now sure, you can go for a walk, ice cream, bowling, skating, even the movies. And if that's what you really want to do, go ahead. But understand this. Statistics and experience show that the dates where you can just sit, relax, and chat are the most effective ones. There it is easier to build real connections and move through stages. The funny thing, the more experience you get, the lazier you get. You stop trying to invent creative dates and just think, I just want to relax, have a drink, and enjoy myself. And usually, that works best. General rule, keep it simple. Of course, if you really want to do something, go for it. After all, one of the main goals of the date is to enjoy it. If you want to eat, pick a cafe or a bar where you can order food. Normally, girls mirror your choice. If you just order drinks, she'll likely do the same. If you order food, offer her to order too. But keep it smart. If you only plan on drinks, don't go to a restaurant. There, it is expected you'll order food. And if you don't smoke, don't pick a shisha bar. First dates don't need to be complicated. Keep it relaxed, keep it simple, and keep it enjoyable.
